Holy One of Israel
HOH-lee one of IZ-ree-uhl
noun
Hebrew Qedosh Yisrael (H6918 + H3478) — the unique title of God overwhelmingly favored by the prophet Isaiah (25 of its 30+ OT occurrences are in Isaiah); combines holiness (the radical otherness of God) with covenantal particularity (the God OF Israel).

See also: Holy One of Israel

Biblical Definition

Holy One of Israel is the signature title of God in the book of Isaiah — appearing 25 times in Isaiah alone (more than in all the rest of the OT combined) and just a handful of times elsewhere (2 Kings 19:22; Pss 71:22; 78:41; 89:18; Jer 50:29; 51:5). The title combines two ideas that the prophets hold together: God's RADICAL OTHERNESS (holiness — separateness, transcendence, moral purity) and His COVENANTAL PARTICULARITY (the God OF Israel — specifically committed to this people, not deity-in-general). Isaiah's prophetic ministry was launched by his vision of the Lord in the temple (Isa 6) where the seraphim cry "Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts" — three-fold holiness, the most intense form of emphasis in Hebrew. From that vision Isaiah carried forward the title that summed up what he had seen: the Holy One who is OF Israel, holy AND committed. The title appears in promises ("Thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel," Isa 41:14; 43:14; 47:4; 48:17; 49:7; 54:5; 55:5; 60:9, 14), in warnings ("They have despised the Holy One of Israel," Isa 1:4; 5:24; 30:11-12, 15), and in exaltations ("thy Maker is thine husband; the LORD of hosts is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Israel," Isa 54:5). The dual-edged use is canonical: the Holy One of Israel is both the GROUND of Israel's hope and the WARNING to Israel's sin. Christ Himself — who is the Servant of the LORD in Isaiah's servant songs (Isa 42, 49, 50, 52-53) — is identified by Peter at Pentecost as "the Holy One" and "the Just" (Acts 3:14). The Holy One of Israel becomes flesh as the Holy One of God.

Webster 1828 Definition

The signature title of God in Isaiah, combining radical holiness with covenantal commitment to Israel; applied to Christ as "the Holy One."

expand to see more

HOLY ONE OF ISRAEL, noun. A Name of God combining His radical holiness (transcendent otherness, moral purity) with His covenantal particularity (commitment to Israel specifically). Hebrew Qedosh Yisrael.

Overwhelmingly favored by Isaiah (25 occurrences in Isaiah, compared to ~5 in the rest of the OT). Originates in Isaiah's temple vision (Isa 6) where the seraphim cry "Holy, holy, holy." Christ identified as "the Holy One" (Acts 3:14; cf. Mark 1:24; Luke 4:34).

Key Scripture

Isaiah 6:3 — "And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory."

Isaiah 41:14 — "Fear not, thou worm Jacob, and ye men of Israel; I will help thee, saith the LORD, and thy redeemer, the Holy One of Israel."

Isaiah 54:5 — "For thy Maker is thine husband; the LORD of hosts is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Israel; The God of the whole earth shall he be called."

Acts 3:14 — "But ye denied the Holy One and the Just, and desired a murderer to be granted unto you."

Modern Corruption

Holy One of Israel is corrupted when the radical otherness is softened to "God is loving" without the awe of holiness, or when the covenantal particularity (the God OF Israel specifically) is dissolved into modernist universalism that loses the gospel's particularity (salvation is from the Jews, John 4:22).

expand to see more

Holiness-softening. Modern theology often emphasizes God's love at the expense of His holiness — "God is love" is true (1 John 4:8) but it is HALF of what 1 John 4 says (4:8 + the entire flow of the letter on righteousness, judgment, and propitiation). The Holy One of Israel is the God WHO IS LOVE AND WHO IS HOLY together — not love at the expense of holiness, not holiness at the expense of love. Isaiah's title preserves both: the Holy One who is THE REDEEMER (love made concrete in covenant rescue). Strip holiness and the love becomes sentimental; strip love and holiness becomes terror. Hold both.

Particularity-dissolution. Modern interfaith and progressive theology often dissolves the "of Israel" particularity — God is the God of all peoples equally, no special covenant with anyone. But the canonical title is specific: the God of ABRAHAM, ISAAC, AND JACOB; the God who chose ISRAEL out of all nations (Deut 7:6-8); the God whose Messiah comes from ISRAEL'S line and offers salvation "to the Jew first, and also to the Greek" (Rom 1:16). The gospel has a particular shape — universal in offer (all are invited), particular in origin (salvation is from the Jews, John 4:22). To dissolve the particularity is to make the gospel a generic spirituality.

Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Qedosh Yisrael (H6918 + H3478) — the Holy One of Israel; Isaiah's signature title for God.

Hebrew Qedosh (H6918) — Holy One; the substantive participle of qadosh (holy)

Hebrew Yisrael (H3478) — Israel; the covenant people; the title binds God to this particular nation

Appears 25 times in Isaiah (more than in all the rest of the OT combined) — Isaiah's signature title

Christ identified as "the Holy One" by Peter (Acts 3:14); by demons (Mark 1:24; Luke 4:34); by John (1 John 2:20)

Usage

"Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts — the seraphim's three-fold cry at Isaiah's commissioning gave him his lifelong title for God."

"Thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel — the Reformed gospel held together: holiness AND redemption in the same Name."

"Christ is the Holy One of Israel become flesh — the radically other God committed to His covenant people, now indwelling them."
